patterns.comment: #wl comments out the whole line, code before it included.
patterns.name: comment.line.number-sign.whole-line.nerve

patterns.comment: #Nl covers N lines counting this one; #Nld this line plus N more. Only the opening line can be matched line-wise.
patterns.name: comment.line.number-sign.multi.nerve

asm-block.comment: inline.ASM { … } runs to the matching brace; inside, the assembly is coloured as assembly: instructions, registers, numbers, labels and comments (ARM64 and x86-64).
asm-block.name: meta.embedded.asm.nerve

text.comment: A text literal is exactly its characters; only \" and \\ escape. A backslash before anything else is literal.
text.name: string.quoted.double.nerve

variable.comment: A quoted name: any printable characters, a `.`, single spaces, and `\'` / `\\` escaped (owner, 2026-10-16): '80%', 'v1.2', 'total due', 'it\'s'. Only a quote that closes on the same line opens one.
variable.name: variable.other.nerve

patterns.comment: `newln`, the newline as a value outside any text (2026-10-07).
patterns.name: constant.character.newline.nerve

patterns.comment: A bare `\n` outside text was the newline's old spelling; it is `newln` since 2026-10-07.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: A whole number in another base, with its word (2026-10-19): binary 1010_0101, hex FF00_00FF, octal 755.
A percentage (2026-10-16): 80%, 12.5%, written with the % on the number.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.percent.nerve

patterns.comment: A percentage written as a word: 80 percent, 12.5 percent.
`*19.99` is `exactly 19.99` (spellings.cyr, 2026-10-16).
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: _ groups digits; , never does. A fraction needs a digit on both sides.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.decimal.nerve

patterns.comment: A collection (2026-10-19): `coll.fn greet { … }`, `coll.handler half_failed { … }`.
`shadow 'x' := 2;` makes a new variable under an old name (2026-10-08), in `let`'s place.
patterns.name: keyword.declaration.nerve

patterns.comment: A language named after a dot (2026-10-02): `extern.C`, `layout.C`, `inline.S` / `inline.ASM`, `inline.MSL`. Not a struct type.
A custom operator, or an operator handed over as a value: `op dot [...]`, `op <+>`, `op div.floor`.
fn name [params] --> type
struct / enum / interface declare a type's bare name.
module declares a namespace.
MAIN is the entry point.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.main.nerve

failure-name.comment: A failure is named after `fail`, both in a signature (`--> T or fail[empty]`) and where it is raised (`fail empty;`).

patterns.comment: A generic blank in angle brackets, optionally constrained by an interface: `<T>`, `<T: Ordered>`.
A generic's bound after its brackets (2026-10-02): `<T>: any`, `<T>: Ordered`.
`|` separates a bound from lifetime groups: `<T>: any | @x`.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.lifetimes.nerve

struct-name.comment: Structs, enums and interfaces are named in PascalCase in the examples; functions are snake_case. A bare capitalised word is therefore a type — including where one is built (`Locker[…]`) or narrowed (`Status.empty`).
struct-name.name: entity.name.type.nerve

field.comment: A struct field or enum case names itself with a bare word before `:`; variables are quoted, so there is no clash.

patterns.comment: A struct field or enum case names itself with a bare word before `:`; variables are quoted, so there is no clash.
A field label when a struct is built: `Locker[number = 1]`. A bare word before a single `=`; assignments name a quoted variable instead.
An enum's case through its type: `Aisle.fresh`, `Status.empty` (a call, `Ticket.next[…]`, is a function).
C's types, each C's size on the machine built for (2026-10-12): `C.int`, `C.long`, `C.size_t`, `C.long_double`.
The base's `optional` (2026-10-09): `optional[int32]`, and its two cases, `optional.none` and `optional.value[…]`.
The brain float, brain16 (2026-10-02). Rust's short names (i8, u8, f64…) and bfloat16 / bf16 are old spellings since 2026-10-07 (#old-spelling); inside a path they are names like any other.
patterns.name: support.type.numeric.nerve

patterns.comment: Integers of any other width, "not standard" (2026-10-07): `not_std.int24`, `not_std.u4`, `not_std.uint256`.
Their old spellings, `!std_int24` and `!std.int24`.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: Widths are explicit: int/uint 8–128, bin 16–64, deci 32–128.
patterns.name: support.type.numeric.nerve

patterns.comment: Text and character types are never bare: str.utf8, char.point.
A library call through a built-in type is one dotted name up to its brackets: list.length[…], str.each.grapheme[…], simd.load.some[…].

patterns.name: support.type.nerve
patterns.comment: The bare built-in types; `any` accepts every type (2026-10-02); `duration` is std's, written bare.
A type written after `:` or `-->` that is none of the above is a struct in this module.
Rounding is one family (2026-10-17): round.near, round.half_up, round.floor, round.ceil, round.trunc.
A kit's prefix before a quoted name: areas::'pi'.
A function's own table limit, in front of it (2026-10-19): `table_bytes 1_024 fn square …`.
A coll.fn member names itself with `named` (2026-10-19).
patterns.name: keyword.other.named.nerve

patterns.comment: `exclude zero` / `include zero` in a C string's bound (2026-10-19).
`exactly 19.99`: an exact deci (2026-10-14), the word for the prefix `*`.
patterns.name: keyword.other.exactly.nerve

patterns.comment: Files included while building, each a const's value (2026-10-12): `incl.bytes[…]`, `incl.str.utf8[…]`, `incl.str.utf16.low_first[…]`; and C headers, through CNC: `incl.C.system["stdio.h"]`, `incl.C["vendor/mylib.h"]`.
`size.of[T]`: its argument is a type, even a C struct's lowercase name (`size.of[tm]`).
A C enum's case through its lowercase name (2026-10-12): `color.BLUE`, `level_t.LOW`.
std's print written bare (std is `bare.optional`): `print.useful[…]`, `print.weird.useful <- …`, `print.useful.stdout[…]`.
`is` gives a case its value (2026-10-07): `paid { is "free"; }`.
patterns.name: keyword.control.nerve

patterns.comment: `my.` is the root of this kit's own paths: `my.'scale'`, and `my.to[]`, a function a keyword's name can't reach otherwise (2026-10-06).
`case.insensitive` / `case.sensitive` are `case.any` / `case.exact` since 2026-10-12.
A kit's marks for its names: `bare.never`, `bare.only`, `bare.optional` (whether the path is needed) and `case.any` / `case.exact` (2026-10-12), optionally for kinds: `[fn, var]`.
Code for one target, chosen when compiling (`on.target aarch64-macos`, `on.target.os windows`, `on.target.chip x86_64`), or when running (`on.machine.chip aarch64`).
A loop's modifiers come right after `for`, the strongest first: `for no_cheat seq 'i' in …`, `for para 'x' in …`. `seq` here is a word, not the type.
`test fn name [] { … }` and its assertions (2026-09-29): `must`, `must.fail` (something fails; `.reason` names which), `must.stop` (a check site fires).
Ownership verbs, at the call site.
patterns.name: keyword.other.ownership.nerve

patterns.comment: An argument's role word (2026-10-14): value, count, key, decimals, bits, exclude…: a lowercase word that opens an argument and has a value after it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.range.label.nerve

patterns.comment: `change` marks every assignment; `let` introduces a binding.
patterns.name: keyword.other.change.nerve

patterns.comment: `immut`, `no_shadow` and `no_cheat` (2026-10-07) say what a name or a loop may not do.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.nerve

patterns.comment: Their old spellings, retired 2026-10-07: `!mut`, `!$`, `!c` / `!cheat`.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: `&` and `&mut` are lend / lend.mut, and lent / lent.mut on a parameter.
patterns.name: keyword.other.ownership.nerve

patterns.comment: Failures in signatures, handled with `otherwise`.
patterns.name: keyword.control.failure.nerve

patterns.comment: `pub.limb`, `pub.neuron` and `pub.strike` are `pub.kit` (spellings.cyr): a library is a kit.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve
keyword.declaration.nerve
patterns.comment: `pub.kit` is `pub` narrowed: visible across the kit.

patterns.name: storage.modifier.nerve
patterns.comment: `to` before a dot is a conversion (to.int32[…]), matched as a call.
`pos` marks a position, in `#strict` files only (removed elsewhere 2026-09-27): 'xs'[pos 1].
patterns.name: keyword.other.position.nerve

patterns.comment: Retired, still reserved so the error can point at the new spelling: var/func, and gives (now is).
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: A capitalised name reached through a module is a type: `counter.Count`, `counter.Count[n = 1]`.
Old prefixes (spellings.cyr): cord and stdkit are std; cca, kin and ricochet are cyjet.
A kit's path: std::print.useful[…]. The :: is a kit's boundary.
A conversion: to.int32[…], to.str.utf8[…].
A struct built with its fields named is a type, even a C struct's lowercase name: `buf[size = 42, count = 7]`.
Calls use brackets, never parentheses: add[1, 2].
A bare lowercase segment between dots, after a bare word, is a module: counter.inner.twice[…]. A quoted variable's field chain starts with ' and is left to the narrowing rule.
A dotted name called with brackets is a function: `counter.bump[…]`, `map.remove[…]`.
A dot narrows: 'xs'.length, str.utf8, lend.mut.
Bitwise: the boolean words narrowed with .bit, plus xor/shl/shr. No precedence — parenthesise.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.bitwise.nerve

patterns.comment: Arithmetic and comparison are words: `plus`, `equal_to`, `at_most` (2026-10-07). `.wrap` wraps, `.ieee` keeps IEEE's -0, div/mod name their rounding; `and.then` / `or.else` stop early.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.nerve

patterns.comment: `$:=` / `$=` shadowed a name until 2026-10-08; it is `shadow 'x' := 2;` now.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: := infers the best type; = needs the type written.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.assignment.infer.nerve

patterns.comment: The long arrows `-->`, `<--`, `<-->` were retired 2026-10-07.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: The arrows are short again (2026-10-07): `->` returns, `<-` feeds `print.weird`, `<->`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arrow.nerve

patterns.comment: A custom operator in brackets, in use: `'u' <+> 'v'`. Not a comparison around a plus.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.custom.nerve

patterns.comment: `'i' += 1;` and the rest, and `'i'++;` / `'i'--;` as a whole statement (2026-10-14): spellings of `change`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.assignment.compound.nerve

patterns.comment: `*const T`, `*mut T` (ptr[T], ptr.mut[T]) and `*'p'` (ptr.read), 2026-10-14.

patterns.name: keyword.operator.pointer.nerve
patterns.comment: `*'p'` reads through a pointer, `change *'p' = v;` writes (2026-10-14); a times between values has spaces round it.
`&&` and `||` are and.then and or.else; a spaced `&` is and (2026-10-14).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.logical.nerve

patterns.comment: `==`, `!=`, `<=`, `>=` are equal_to, not_equal, at_most, at_least (2026-10-14).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.comparison.nerve

patterns.comment: `**` is pow; `+`, `*`, `/`, `%` are plus, times, div.trunc, mod.trunc (2026-10-14).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arithmetic.nerve

patterns.comment: ++ joins text.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.join.nerve

patterns.comment: Retired 2026-10-07: `==`, `!==`, `</==`, `>/==` are `equal_to`, `not_equal`, `at_most`, `at_least`.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: `<` and `>` stay glyphs; the rest of comparison is words (2026-10-07).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.comparison.nerve

patterns.comment: Retired spellings; `/` is now a named division and `<==` / `>==` are `</==` / `>/==`.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: Retired since 2026-10-03: `+` is `plus`, and `+~` / `-~` are `plus.wrap` / `minus.wrap`.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: A negative keeps the `-` sign; binary arithmetic uses words.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arithmetic.nerve
keyword.operator.assignment.nerve
patterns.comment: A lone `=`: a written type's value, a change, or a field label. A longer run is an operator.
A maximal run of operator characters is one operator: the language's own, or a custom `op`.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.custom.nerve

patterns.comment: A variadic parameter.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.variadic.nerve

enum-body.comment: Inside `enum Name { … }` every bare word is a case; a case with a payload is written `some: <T>`, and in a `layout.c enum` a case is given its number: `a = 65`.

patterns.comment: `layout.c enum Key { a = 65 }`: each case's number (2026-09-27).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.assignment.nerve

case-arm.comment: An arm of `match` or of an `otherwise { … }` handler names an enum case or a failure: a bare word, optionally binding a quoted variable, before `{`. Keywords that open a block (`else`, `loop`, `concur`…) are matched earlier and win. A word straight after a value is an operator position (`'a' and 'b' {`), never an arm, so that position is excluded.

unit.comment: A unit after a number: durations (`5 seconds`, `1500 millis`) and a text bound's unit (`[1, 40 graphemes]`). Lists are oracle/src/parser.rs DURATION_UNITS and the text-bound units.

bound.comment: `min` / `max` as an open end of a ranged type: `int32[1, max]`, `int32[min, 100]`.

word-operator.comment: A bare word between two values is a custom infix operator: `'u' dot 'v'`. Keywords at the same place (`in`) are matched earlier and win.

module-path.comment: A lowercase bare word before `.` is a module: `counter.Count`, `counter.inner.twice`. The parser enforces lowercase module names. Built-in types before a dot (`str.utf8`, `map.remove`) are matched earlier.

function-ref.comment: Variables are always quoted, so a bare lowercase word left over is a function named as a value: `first_by[…, by_number]`, `let 'f' := by_number;`.
function-ref.name: entity.name.function.reference.nerve

strict.comment: `#strict` was retired 2026-10-07; what it wrote out is every file's now.
strict.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: The check tiers: `check`, `no_check` (2026-10-07), and NO_FUCKING_CHECKS, which also trusts the numbers C hands back.
patterns.name: keyword.other.check.nerve

patterns.comment: `nocheck` and `!check` are `no_check` since 2026-10-07.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

lifetime.comment: `@x` names a lifetime group on a returned borrow, `--> lent@x T`.

patterns.comment: The old `level.when_chained.left_first 2` (spellings.zv).
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: Inside a level, every word names an operator.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.word.custom.nerve

patterns.comment: …and every run of symbols does too.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.custom.nerve

register.comment: A register an inline block reads or writes: `with ['n' -> rax, 'n' <- rax]`.

empty-value.comment: An empty text, map or list (2026-10-14: `str.empty`, as `map.empty`).

old-spelling.comment: The old spellings spellings.zv lists (76 rows, 2026-10-15), shown as errors where the language refuses them, each only in the place its row names: a type name outside a path, an operator between values, a word after `inline.`.

patterns.comment: The symbols spellings.cyr retires (2026-10-16): == != <= >= are equal_to not_equal at_most at_least; / and % between values are div.X and mod.X; && || are and.then or.else; & is `and` between values and lend/lent before one; * is x, ** is xx, *const *mut are ptr / ptr.mut, a prefix * reads a pointer or marks exactly; ++ -- += -= *= /= %= **= are spelled with change. `<`, `>`, `+`, `-`, `x`, `xx` and the arrows stay. Percentages (80%) are numbers, matched before reaching here.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: Old kit-manager prefixes and words: ricochet::, kin::, cca:: are cyjet::; collection. is coll.fn / coll.handler.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: `for no_cheat` is `no_cheat for` (2026-10-18): the word goes in front.
std::round / floor / ceil / trunc are the round.X family (2026-10-17).
A dependency says its kind (2026-10-19): cyjet::dep[…] is cyjet::dep.path[…] or cyjet::dep.reg[…]; cyjet::dep.std is cyjet::dep.path.std[…].
A simd type's lane count says `count` (2026-10-19): simd[int32, 4] is simd[int32, count 4].
Rust's and short number names: int8 and the rest, outside a path (not after :: or .).
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: The same after a kit's path, as std::print.useful.auto_newline.
giveS and gives are `is`; auto_newline is auto_newln.

patterns.comment: giveS is `is`; neuron and strike are `kit`; `limb.` is `my.` and `pub.limb` / `pub.strike` are `pub.kit`. A bare `limb` is current: a compiler extension (cyjet::limb).
inline.Assembly, inline.S, inline.LLVM and the long names are inline.ASM, inline.LL, inline.MSL.
x~ and xx~ are times.wrap and pow.wrap; x and xx themselves are the current symbols (2026-10-16).
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: The arrows past the short ones, and the comparisons with = tacked on: -> and <- (and <->) are the only arrows; != <= >= or the words.

patterns.comment: ! in front of a value is `not`; between two values it is a custom operator (op_bang.zg).
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: $:= and $= are shadow.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: A manifest's cores, lobes and plugins are its limbs.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: level.when_chained is `level 2 { plus, minus } left_first`.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: A bare \n among a print's values is newln. Inside a text it stays text (print.format's \n is its own).
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

patterns.comment: `neg` is `negate` (spellings.cyr), `neg.ieee` too.
patterns.name: invalid.deprecated.nerve

symbol-word.comment: `x` (times) and `xx` (pow) are the current symbols (2026-10-16), between values; never a field (`x: …`), a named argument (`x = …`) or a name ('x', @x, .x). `negate` is a prefix word.
